name: Richard Blumenthal
stance: Wants mandatory independent testing and federal oversight of frontier AI models, as in his AI Risk Evaluation Act with Hawley.

statements.text: Co-introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act (S. 2938) with Sen. Hawley.
AI companies have rushed to market with products that are unsafe for the public and often lack basic due diligence and testing.
There is widespread public support for sensible safeguards on AI & strong interest in the Senate for reforms & rules.
Humongous AI investor SoftBank donated $50 million to Trump’s presidential library & foundation just before Trump withdrew his AI regulatory Executive Order.
We need to know beforehand if the next OpenAI & Anthropic release will empower hackers & foreign adversaries.
The White House should go further to require AI companies contracting with the federal government participate & expand the program to other forms of weaponization.
AI safety requires Congressional action—as many seem to believe, but avoid supporting specifics. The Hawley-Blumenthal framework provides a good beginning.
Big Tech can never be trusted to supervise itself, especially when trillions of dollars of investments & potential profits are at stake.
Incidents like the hacking of Hugging Face show that we need an independent federal agency scrutinizing AI models & doing NTSB-like investigations of failures.

In the face of a stunning failure, OpenAI appears to be taking steps that prioritize the performance and profit of its A.I. models with the knowledge that those changes could be detrimental to public safety.
Sent OpenAI eight questions on containment failures in the Hugging Face breach and on the release of a less-monitorable model, with a September 24, 2026 deadline.
OpenAI’s rogue bots threaten civil privacy, national security, & public safety.
It must be a statutorily established regimen, with power to determine whether models & new products are safe & effective, just as independent scientists are authorized to do under the FDA.
OpenAI, Meta & Anthropic must be held legally accountable for their rogue, dangerous AI agents, including through my AI Risk Evaluation Act.
